latest_commit.subject: docs: PLAN for discriminating the BP stall class (real hesitation vs encoder blindness)
latest_commit.body:
Writes up the open question from #68 as an actionable plan: hypothesis
(a) real rotor hesitation, with supply sag from the CPU flash+radio
burst as the leading non-mechanical candidate, vs (b) the rotor kept
turning and the ULP went blind (#48 SENS_IOMUX_CLK_EN class). Records
what is already settled (same-binary run-011 comparison, the ~16x
detector sensitivity change across the fold, all 7 stalls in
BP_RUNNING, seg_recover's cold restart) and the owner's correction that
the devboard park is NOT a hard spot, so mechanical drag is retracted
as an explanation.

Decisive experiment: capture whether encoder edges were still accruing
at the instant the stall is declared — an edge-counter witness in the
FAULT payload (works in the field, forever), plus a bench drive with an
independent rotation witness and a must-fail control. Decision table
maps each outcome to its consequence; if (b) proves out, #68 becomes
urgent because seg_recover would be stopping healthy motors.

Prerequisites recorded: finish + conclude the running field test, and
remove /crumbs_on (a confound armed for the #67 hunt that run 011 did
not have).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
